summary: Eight concrete, comment-endorsed tools and projects surfaced from a complete 30-story HN front-page crawl.
telegram_footer: 8 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Testafize
items.summary: A Python-project template that establishes tests and automated checks before coding.
items.why_included: A commenter described repeat use for generated projects and a successful Python 2 migration.
items.evidence: One developer uses Testafize as a starting template and reports that its check workflow also helped migrate an old Python 2 script.

evidence_sources.author: tingletech
evidence_sources.excerpt: I have a template I use with generated python projects that sets up all the test info first. https://github.com/brian-learns/testafize

items.name: Numba
items.source_story_title: Numba in the Browser: Unlocking a New Scientific Python Stack in JupyterLite
items.summary: A Python JIT compiler for writing NumPy-like code with native-speed execution.
items.why_included: A detailed first-hand endorsement explained its practical performance-versus-ergonomics trade-off.
items.evidence: A commenter praised Numba for letting them retain a NumPy-like workflow while getting bytecode-level performance, while noting its sizable installation footprint.

evidence_sources.author: momojo
evidence_sources.excerpt: Numba is a little magic because you get to write stuff that feels like numpy, but get literal bytecode perf.

items.name: tinygrad
items.source_story_title: Chestnut – eGPU dock with open-source firmware
items.summary: A lightweight neural-network framework for running deep-learning workloads across hardware.
items.why_included: A user gave a clear cross-platform, first-hand reliability endorsement.
items.evidence: A commenter said the setup works well with tinygrad across Mac, Windows, and Linux.

evidence_sources.author: rvz
evidence_sources.excerpt: I can rest assured that when I use this on any machine running Mac, Windows or Linux, I know it just works well with tinygrad.

items.name: Tess's Android Wayland Compositor
items.summary: An Android Wayland compositor project for running Linux desktop applications on Android.
items.why_included: The project received direct positive reaction for its potential on foldable devices.
items.evidence: A commenter called the compositor cool and highlighted the prospect of running interesting applications on foldables.

evidence_sources.author: alex7o
evidence_sources.excerpt: Oh that Is cool especially on a foldable you can run some interesting apps on it.

items.name: CircuitJS
items.summary: A browser-based circuit simulator for interactive electronics prototyping and probing.
items.why_included: A regular user gave a specific workflow comparison against SPICE simulators.
items.evidence: A commenter regularly uses CircuitJS for prototyping because components can be modified and probed in real time, then uses SPICE for final checking.

evidence_sources.author: peterus
evidence_sources.excerpt: He also made circuitjs, a very useful circuit simulator which I regularly use for prototyping.

items.name: Nightscout
items.source_story_title: SugarTrack – an offline Android logbook for blood sugar (no account, no cloud)
items.summary: A self-hostable platform for viewing and managing continuous glucose-monitor data.
items.why_included: The recommendation was specific about self-hosting and practical glucose-monitor support.
items.evidence: A commenter called Nightscout an awesome self-hostable tool for continuous glucose-monitor workflows.

evidence_sources.author: VoidWhisperer
evidence_sources.excerpt: Nightscout is an awesome tool because it can be self-hosted

items.name: Everything is a Remix
items.source_story_title: Patterns and problems in emerging multi-agent systems
items.summary: A video essay series about creativity, influence, and the reuse of existing ideas.
items.why_included: It received an unambiguous recommendation as useful context for understanding creative work.
items.evidence: A commenter highly recommended the series as a way to see how creative work combines existing material.

evidence_sources.author: alexpotato
evidence_sources.excerpt: I would highly recommend the "Everything is a Remix" series on YouTube

items.name: Mic Drop
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Mic Drop, a real-time multiplayer karaoke game
items.summary: A real-time multiplayer karaoke game for performing with friends online.
items.why_included: A commenter independently reacted positively and expressed intent to try it with a friend.
items.evidence: A commenter called Mic Drop very cool and said they would find a friend to play with.
